claims.text: A machine-learning-based method can predict fusion and high-temperature thermodynamic properties of high-entropy systems.
The proposed method can predict free energies of solid and fluid states.
The proposed method can predict relevant entropy terms.
Machine-learning algorithms can learn relationships among composition, processing history, and properties of high-entropy systems.
Learning composition–processing–property relationships enables prediction of free energies and entropy terms.
The machine-learning method would reduce the cost of obtaining fusion and high-temperature thermodynamic properties relative to explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics workflows and TOR-TILD.
The machine-learning method would reduce computational complexity relative to explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics workflows and TOR-TILD.
The machine-learning method could be faster than explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics workflows and TOR-TILD.
The machine-learning method could have improved fidelity relative to explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics workflows and TOR-TILD.
The proposed scope includes elemental, binary, and multicomponent systems.
The proposed temperature domain is high temperature near phase transitions.
The method should be evaluated by comparing its free energies, entropy terms, and derived thermodynamic properties against explicit ab initio molecular dynamics, TOR-TILD, and experiment.
Additional training data or algorithm refinement may be required for multicomponent high-entropy systems.

contradictions.description: Elemental and binary systems are described as included within 'high-entropy systems,' although the hypothesis does not define how elemental systems, and binary systems generally, qualify as high-entropy systems.
